course.title: IELTS Starter: Everyday Topics
course.description: Band 4.0–5.0. Familiar topics, IELTS question types and short answers, written for IeltsWithHarry.

lessons.title: Food and cooking words
lessons.summary: Words for meals, tastes and cooking methods.

material.introduction:
Food questions are common in Speaking Part 1, and cooking steps often appear in Writing Task 1 process diagrams. Learn words for tastes (spicy, sour) and for cooking methods (boil, fry, steam) so you can describe dishes clearly.

Mẹo: khi tả món ăn, nêu nguyên liệu + cách nấu + vị: 'steamed fish with a sour sauce'.

vocabulary.definition: One of the foods you use to make a dish.
vocabulary.example: Rice noodles are the main ingredient in pho.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Món này cần năm nguyên liệu.

vocabulary.definition: Having a strong, hot taste from chilli or spices.
vocabulary.example: Food in central Vietnam is often very spicy.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Tôi không thích đồ ăn cay.
acceptedSentences: I do not like spicy food.

vocabulary.definition: Having a sharp taste like a lemon.
vocabulary.example: This soup is a little sour because it has tamarind.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Quả chanh này rất chua.

vocabulary.definition: To cook something in very hot water.
vocabulary.example: Boil the eggs for eight minutes.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Mẹ tôi luộc rau mỗi tối.
acceptedSentences: My mother boils vegetables every evening.
My mum boils vegetables every evening.

vocabulary.definition: To cook something in hot oil.
vocabulary.example: We fry the spring rolls until they are golden.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Đừng chiên cá quá lâu.
acceptedSentences: Don't fry the fish for too long.
Do not fry the fish for too long.

vocabulary.definition: To cook something using the hot air from boiling water.
vocabulary.example: Steamed fish is healthier than fried fish.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Tôi thích cá hấp.

vocabulary.definition: Eating the right amounts of different kinds of food.
vocabulary.example: A balanced diet includes vegetables, protein and grains.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Học sinh cần một chế độ ăn cân bằng.
acceptedSentences: Students need to have a balanced diet.

vocabulary.definition: Food that is cooked and sold outside, often at stalls.
vocabulary.example: Hanoi is famous for its street food.
vocabulary.sentencePromptVi: Viết bằng tiếng Anh: Đồ ăn đường phố ở đây rẻ và ngon.
acceptedSentences: The street food here is cheap and delicious.
Street food here is cheap and delicious.

lessons.title: Countable and uncountable nouns
lessons.summary: Use a/an, some, any, many, much and a lot of with food nouns.

material.rule:
Countable nouns have singular and plural forms: an egg – two eggs, a banana – some bananas.
Uncountable nouns have no plural and no a/an: rice, water, bread, milk, meat, advice, information.

• some – positive sentences: I bought some apples / some rice.
• any – negatives and questions: We don't have any eggs. Is there any milk?
• many + plural countable: How many eggs? (not many)
• much + uncountable: How much sugar? (not much)
• a lot of – both: a lot of vegetables, a lot of water.
• To count uncountable nouns, use containers: a bottle of water, a bowl of rice, a slice of bread.

Ghi nhớ: How many + danh từ đếm được; How much + danh từ không đếm được.
material.example: How much rice do we need, and are there any onions left?

questions.prompt: How ___ water do you drink every day?

options: I'd like a slice of bread, please.
questions.explanation: 'bread' không đếm được; dùng 'a slice of bread'.

questions.prompt: There aren't ___ tomatoes in the fridge.
questions.explanation: Câu phủ định với danh từ đếm được số nhiều → any.
Có thể nói 'a carrot / two carrots'; sugar và milk không đếm được.

questions.prompt: We need ___ eggs for the cake – about six.
questions.explanation: Câu khẳng định với danh từ số nhiều → some.

questions.prompt: Can you give me some ___ about healthy eating?
questions.explanation: 'advice' là danh từ không đếm được – không thêm -s, không dùng 'an'.

lessons.title: A morning at the floating market
lessons.summary: Read about a market and complete sentences with words from the text.

material.passage:
The floating market at Cai Rang, near Can Tho, starts long before sunrise. By five o'clock, hundreds of boats are already moving slowly along the river. Each boat hangs a sample of what it sells from a tall bamboo pole, so buyers can see from a distance whether a boat has pineapples, pumpkins or sweet potatoes.

Most of the sellers are farmers or wholesalers who buy fruit and vegetables from gardens upstream. They sell in large quantities to shop owners and restaurant cooks, who then take the produce to markets on land. Tourists can still buy a single mango or a bag of rambutans, but the market is mainly a place for business.

Smaller boats move between the big ones, selling breakfast. A woman in a boat no wider than a bed can serve hot noodle soup, iced coffee and sticky rice without spilling a drop. Visitors say that eating soup on a gently moving boat is the most memorable part of the morning.

The market is changing. As new roads and bridges connect the villages, more trade happens by truck, and the number of boats has fallen. Local authorities now hope that tourism will help the market survive, and they have built a new pier where visitors can take short boat tours.

questions.prompt: Complete: Each boat shows what it sells by hanging a sample from a tall ______.
questions.explanation: 'hangs a sample of what it sells from a tall bamboo pole'.
questions.evidence: hangs a sample of what it sells from a tall bamboo pole

questions.prompt: Who are the main customers at the market?
questions.explanation: Người bán bán số lượng lớn 'to shop owners and restaurant cooks'. Du khách vẫn mua được nhưng không phải khách chính.
questions.evidence: They sell in large quantities to shop owners and restaurant cooks

questions.prompt: Complete: The small breakfast boats are no wider than a ______.
questions.explanation: 'a boat no wider than a bed'.
questions.evidence: a boat no wider than a bed

questions.prompt: According to visitors, the most memorable part is…
options: eating soup on a moving boat
questions.explanation: 'eating soup on a gently moving boat is the most memorable part of the morning'.
questions.evidence: eating soup on a gently moving boat is the most memorable part of the morning

questions.prompt: Why has the number of boats fallen?
questions.explanation: Đường và cầu mới giúp buôn bán bằng xe tải nhiều hơn.
questions.evidence: more trade happens by truck, and the number of boats has fallen

questions.prompt: Complete: Authorities have built a new ______ for boat tours.
questions.explanation: 'they have built a new pier where visitors can take short boat tours'.
questions.evidence: they have built a new pier where visitors can take short boat tours

lessons.title: A cooking class
lessons.summary: Listen to a chef and match each step with the right detail.

material.transcript:
Chef: Good evening, everyone. Tonight we're making fresh spring rolls, and they're much easier than they look.
First, boil the rice noodles for just three minutes, then put them in cold water so they don't stick together.
While the noodles are cooling, boil the prawns. They only need about two minutes – when they turn pink, they're ready. Cut each prawn in half along its length.
Next, prepare the vegetables. Wash the lettuce and the herbs – we're using mint and Thai basil – and cut the cucumber into thin strips.
Now the important part: the rice paper. Dip one sheet into warm water for about two seconds only. If you leave it longer, it becomes too soft and breaks.
Put the lettuce and noodles near the bottom of the paper, then three prawn halves in the middle, with the pink side facing down. Fold in the sides and roll it up tightly.
Finally, the sauce. Mix two spoons of peanut butter with hoisin sauce and a little warm water. Some people add chilli, but I'll leave that to you.
Any questions? No? Then let's start rolling!

questions.prompt: How long should you boil the rice noodles?
questions.explanation: 'boil the rice noodles for just three minutes' – hai phút là thời gian luộc tôm.

questions.prompt: How do you know the prawns are ready?
Which herbs does the chef use?
What happens if the rice paper stays in water too long?
options: It becomes too soft and breaks.

questions.prompt: What is the sauce mainly made from?
questions.explanation: 'Mix two spoons of peanut butter with hoisin sauce'. Ớt là tùy chọn.

lessons.title: Describe how to make a dish
lessons.summary: Write 80–100 words explaining the steps of a simple recipe.

material.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining how to make a simple dish from your country. Describe the steps in order and use sequencing words (first, next, after that, while, finally). Mention the ingredients and at least two cooking methods (boil, fry, steam, grill…).
material.modelAnswer: Egg fried rice is quick and cheap to make. First, cook some rice and let it cool, because cold rice fries better. Next, chop an onion and a few spring onions. After that, heat some oil in a large pan and fry the onion for two minutes. While the onion is cooking, beat two eggs in a bowl. Then pour the eggs into the pan and stir them quickly. Add the rice and a little fish sauce, and fry everything for five minutes. Finally, sprinkle the spring onions on top and serve hot.
checklist: Introduce the dish in one sentence
Put the steps in a clear order
Use at least four sequencing words
Use countable/uncountable nouns correctly (some rice, two eggs)

lessons.title: Talking about eating habits
lessons.summary: Answer Part 1 questions about food and meals.

material.prompt:
IELTS Speaking Part 1 – answer each question in 2–3 sentences:
1. What is your favourite food? Why?
2. Do you usually eat at home or in restaurants?
3. Can you cook? What can you make?
4. Do you think people in your country eat more healthily now than in the past?
material.modelAnswer: My favourite food is bun cha, grilled pork with rice noodles and herbs, because the sauce is sweet and a little sour at the same time. On weekdays I usually eat at home with my family, but at the weekend we often try a new restaurant. I can cook a few simple dishes, like fried rice and omelettes. I think people know more about healthy eating now, but they also eat much more fast food than in the past.
checklist: Name the food and describe its taste
Compare past and present in question 4
Use food vocabulary from this unit
Listen again: did each answer have a reason?
